## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Assumption practitioners usually hold | If it were false, the conditional effect would be… |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Inside the cell, the 0→3 skip is redundant because the macro skeleton already has inter-stage residuals. | An in-cell skip on edge 3 still matters. It would let deeper serial convs (edges 0, 2, 5) gain more. |
| A2 | An avg_pool edit has the same effect wherever it sits, whatever surrounds it. | Pool damage depends on whether a parallel identity or conv route can carry the high-frequency signal. Neighbouring edges would then modulate the cost. |
| A3 | Parallel 3×3 convs into node 3 add capacity independently (width helps, roughly additively). | They saturate. A second 3×3 into the output gains less when one already exists. |
| A4 | Receptive field comes only from the edited edge's own kernel. | Upstream 3×3s or pools supply spatial context. Downgrading edge 5 to 1×1 would then be cheaper when they are present. |
| A5 | Edge importance is fixed: serial edges matter and shortcut edges are minor. | Importance shifts with topology. When a route into node 3 is cut, the remaining edges become bottlenecks and their upgrades gain more. |
| A6 | Skip connections are always benign additions. | A skip can dilute a conv route at the summing node, or rescue it. Either way its value depends on what it sits beside. |
| A7 | 1×1 convs are cheap, neutral fillers. | Stacked 1×1s give no spatial mixing. A 1×1 edit would be worse when the next serial edge is also 1×1. |
| A8 | Interactions are dataset-specific: CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120 are "capacity hungry" and CIFAR-10 is not. | Interactions driven by topology carry over consistently across all three datasets. |

## Hypotheses

Each hypothesis pairs two different edges. No condition setting is used more than twice. No condition makes the edited edge inert; for example, I never condition edits on edges 2 or 4 on edge 0 being none.
